key_insight: For CBCT-based TMJ osteoarthritis detection, the biggest performance gain came from partially unfreezing the final two transformer blocks of a self-supervised ViT rather than from the specific DINO backbone alone.
clinical_relevance: This suggests foundation models can be adapted effectively for low-data dental/maxillofacial imaging, potentially improving automated screening of subtle TMJ OA changes on CBCT.
method: Axial CBCT slices were encoded with DINO-family ViT backbones and combined with attention-based multiple instance learning (MIL) for patient-level classification.
The study compared frozen versus partially adapted backbones across DINOv1, DINOv2, DINOv2+reg, and RAD-DINO.
Ablations tested different unfreezing strategies and aggregation designs on a multi-source CBCT dataset.
evidence_signal: On the study dataset, fully frozen DINOv2 reached AUC 0.671, while unfreezing the final two blocks raised AUC to 0.902, outperforming DINOv1, DINOv2+reg, and a supervised ImageNet ViT-B/16 baseline.
watch_item: Results come from a specific multi-source CBCT setting, so generalization and site-specific performance may still require external validation before deployment.
paper_title: Self-Supervised Vision Transformers for CBCT-Based Detection of Temporomandibular Joint Osteoarthritis
